title: Bassist Jimmy Johnson, string bass and drums
summary: Jimmy Johnson was an old but strong ear player; the band was among the first to use string bass, adding Harold Holmes. Talk drifts to his bicycle and a drummer's plain drum set.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Yeah. All planned in the front. Right. Well, what about somebody like Jimmy Johnson? He couldn't have been young. The bass player? The bass player.
No, Jimmy was an old man.
But was he in shape enough to travel?

Sure he was. He was in beautiful health. He was a strong old man. And he still drank his whiskey, but he never was drunk on the job that I can remember. But Jimmy was strong, as strong as anyone in the band had to be to play the way he played. See, my band is one of the first bands to use a string bass. And I finally got two string basses in the band. Jimmy Johnson and Harold Holmes. Well, Harold was a different type of bass player. He was more modern than Jimmy, but Jimmy was more of a true bass player than he was. What do you mean? When I say true, I mean his notes were more perfect. And Harold would make a lot of notes, while Jimmy made just a few notes. But they sounded different and fill in a little bit more. And then, too, Harold was writing a lot of arrangements.
Well, Jimmy Johnson must have had a good ear then.
He did. He was mostly an ear player from the old days. But finally Jimmy did learn how to read bass parts enough to read bass parts.
Did you ever see him on a bicycle? Somebody was telling me he used to even ride a bicycle.

Well, if it was, it was in the days that he was playing here with Bunk Jones, not with Bunk, with what's the trumpet player, the first one? Buddy Bowling. Buddy Bowling. Maybe in those days he might have been a younger man. He might have rode a bicycle then. You mean with that bass on his back? Yeah. Yes, I've heard him say that. I mentioned Larry Cottrell's daddy yesterday at the concert. I used to lug those drums all the way from his house up to Clay Hall Street. And then there was a whole set of drums on his back.
Well, he had special drums, too, though, they said.
Well, not necessarily so. I never seen anything special about the drums. He had the same drums all the time. Oh, yeah. In those times.
Sure. They were just a regular set of drums.
Regular set of drums. Not collapsible or like that. Oh, no. Nothing in those days like that. But all in all, the concert yesterday was the best this year. What do you think about it?
